tasks.short: Learn to use new office tools for everyday administrative work.

steps.what: Read release notices and user guides, and make learning notes.

loop.input: Approved release notices and user guides for the relevant version.
loop.output: Source-linked learning notes covering changed functions and practice suggestions.
loop.check: Check source links, version and coverage; the learner verifies important instructions.
loop.stop: One extraction and one validation retry per document; unsupported instructions return to manual reading.
loop.why_not_simpler: Guides describe changes in free text; fixed parsing misses their meaning.

steps.what: Agree which changes matter and choose practice exercises with a trainer.
Practise routine booking and filing exercises using fictitious records.
Check practice results against the task checklist and confirm readiness.
Record completion and remaining learning needs.

tasks.design: A portable learning pack in {DOCS} combines task checklists with source-linked notes drafted from approved guides by a bounded model loop. The learner practises in {CALENDAR} and {DOCS}; configured completion tracking in {LMS} records the trainer's readiness decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful instructions were scattered across long guides, while relevance and practical competence required personal assessment.
tasks.enabler_now: Bounded extraction can shorten reading, and existing learning features can track completion. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of assembling reusable practice packs.
tasks.still_hard: Learning requires practice. Version changes, unfamiliar permissions and poorly documented local procedures still cause rework.
tasks.human_edge: The learner builds practical confidence and notices when an instruction does not fit the real workflow.

ambition.what: A monthly office-tool practice clinic for occasional users.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into finding instructions and recording completion; practice remains central. Decision rights stay the same.

reach.task: Turn recurring user difficulties into clear change requirements.
reach.learn: Describe reproducible problems, permission dependencies and acceptance criteria.

evidence.claim: Source-linked learning notes can reduce preparation, but reading assistance does not replace practical learning.
The step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured outcomes.

assumptions: The baseline is an occasional office-tool rollout with guides, practical exercises and completion recording.
The learner can begin with approved documents and fictitious practice records before any integration.
GDPR applies to identifiable learning records. Consultation follows national rules where applicable; no staff monitoring or automated employee assessment is introduced.
Build ranges cover a small pilot. Access and any employee consultation may overlap other work and can exceed the estimate.
unknowns: Which tools and versions the learner must use.
Whether an LMS is used for office-tool learning.
Who confirms readiness and what completion evidence is required.
Whether local consultation requirements apply to the proposed learning records.
research_questions: Which short practice formats best retain skills used only occasionally?
How reliably can source-linked extraction distinguish versions and permission-dependent instructions?
new_work: Check extracted instructions and repair broken source links.
Refresh exercises after interface or permission changes.
Maintain fictitious practice records and handle unresolved questions.

tasks.short: Help colleagues use office tools and teach routine computer tasks.

steps.what: Collect the colleague's question, affected tool and relevant error details.
Observe the problem and distinguish training needs from technical faults.
Prepare instructions suited to the colleague's task and experience.

loop.input: Support assessment and approved instructions for the relevant tool version.
loop.output: A short support guide with source links and explicit escalation points.
loop.check: Verify each instruction against its source; the assistant checks applicability before sharing.
loop.stop: One draft and one revision; missing sources or permission changes go to the support team.
loop.why_not_simpler: Adapting free-text instructions to an unfamiliar question requires language interpretation; exact matches reuse existing guides.

steps.what: Demonstrate the task, let the colleague practise and answer questions.
Record the outcome and route unresolved faults to the support team.

tasks.design: A configured form in {HELPDESK} captures the support brief and retrieves matching approved instructions from {DOCS}. A bounded drafting loop adapts instructions when needed, while the assistant approves the guide, coaches the colleague and confirms an outcome that drives configured recording and routing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Questions arrived without essential details, instructions were repeatedly rewritten, and coaching depended on the colleague's confidence and context.
tasks.enabler_now: Forms, searchable approved guides and outcome routing are established capabilities. Bounded drafting makes tailoring instructions cheaper without requiring an autonomous support agent.
tasks.still_hard: People may struggle to describe problems or fear making mistakes. Device faults, access changes and unsafe workarounds require the support team.
tasks.human_edge: Patient observation reveals misunderstanding, anxiety and accessibility needs that a written answer can miss.

ambition.what: Short office-tool coaching sessions for shift staff who miss daytime training.

tasks.altitude: The assistant spends less time gathering details and rewriting instructions, and more time coaching. Technical access and policy decisions remain with the support team.

reach.task: Analyse recurring support requests to identify usability problems.
reach.learn: Separate training gaps from defects and write reproducible problem reports.

evidence.claim: Structured intake, reusable instructions and configured routing can reduce support administration; coaching remains substantially human.
The digest provides no directly matching case measuring general office-tool coaching gains.
The step shares, remaining effort and build ranges require pilot validation.

assumptions: The assistant provides everyday application help and refers technical faults to a support team.
A portable intake form and approved guide library can be used before connecting a helpdesk.
Screenshots and examples exclude passwords and unnecessary personal data; GDPR applies to support records.
Consultation follows national rules where applicable. The design does not score employees or monitor their computer usage.
Build ranges cover one support queue and a small guide library; formal consultation may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which requests the assistant is authorised to resolve.
Whether a helpdesk exists and accepts configured forms and routing.
Which instructions are approved and who maintains them.
What accessibility needs, retention rules and consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Which intake questions reduce follow-up without discouraging less confident users?
How accurately do adapted guides preserve prerequisites and escalation instructions?
new_work: Remove outdated instructions and maintain version labels.
Review failed routing and repeated unresolved questions.
Keep support examples free of unnecessary personal data.

tasks.short: Replenish office supplies, receive deliveries and hand supplies to colleagues.

steps.what: Inspect cupboards and count supplies running low.
Combine stock counts and colleague requests into a replenishment list.
Select catalogue items and create a purchase requisition.
Approve the requisition against budget and purchasing limits.
Send the approved purchase order to the supplier.
Receive the delivery and check quantities, items and damage.
Enter received quantities and delivery exceptions.
Put supplies away and hand requested items to colleagues.

tasks.design: Configure catalogue requests, stock-count forms and reorder thresholds in {PROCUREMENT}, removing the separate replenishment list in {SPREADSHEET}. Approved requisitions produce supplier orders, and structured receiving checks produce goods receipts; people count, inspect and distribute the supplies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requests, physical counts and purchasing records were disconnected. Small order values made additional setup seem disproportionate.
tasks.enabler_now: Catalogue rules, approval routing and receiving forms are established capabilities. Configuration and inexpensive connectors can join them without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Physical stock accuracy, damaged deliveries, substitutions and changing consumption still need attention. Supplier interfaces may limit automatic ordering.
tasks.human_edge: The assistant notices physical shortages, unsuitable substitutions and urgent needs before the records reflect them.

ambition.what: A weekly replenishment review for fast-moving office consumables.

tasks.altitude: Less time goes into consolidating requests and re-entering orders and receipts. Physical handling continues, and spending approval stays with the budget owner.

reach.task: Set stock thresholds and investigate recurring stock discrepancies.
reach.learn: Use lead times, demand variation and cycle counts to set practical replenishment levels.

evidence.claim: Catalogue replenishment, approval routing and receipt posting are established deterministic purchasing patterns.
Physical counting, inspection and distribution remain human even when purchasing administration is automated.
The step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates; the digest contains no matching purchasing case.

assumptions: The baseline uses a shared replenishment list alongside a purchasing system and physical cupboards.
Routine consumables have approved catalogue items and suppliers; exceptions enter a manual queue.
Purchase approval authorises only the approved items, quantities and price limits. Changes require renewed approval before dispatch.
The future receiving form captures checks during physical inspection, removing later re-entry.
Low-value supplies are counted periodically rather than tracked individually at every issue.
GDPR applies to named request records. National consultation rules are checked if the design changes employee monitoring or working arrangements.
Build ranges cover one catalogue and order channel; access delays can extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Whether purchasing supports stock thresholds, structured receiving and supplier order dispatch.
Which suppliers, catalogue items, spending limits and approval routes apply.
Whether supply issues require individual tracking.
How often substitutions, delivery discrepancies and urgent purchases occur.
Which access permissions and national consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: How well do periodic counts support replenishment for shared, untracked cupboards?
Which catalogue controls prevent duplicate orders and obsolete-item substitutions?
new_work: Maintain catalogue items, reorder thresholds and supplier lead times.
Resolve rejected orders, substitutions and delivery discrepancies.
Check duplicate prevention and failed dispatches.
Periodically reconcile stock balances with physical counts.

tasks.short: Prepare invitations, flyers and other conference or event materials.

steps.what: Collect event details, audience requirements and approved assets from the organiser.
Draft invitation or flyer copy from the event brief.

loop.input: Validated event brief, audience description, approved wording and length limits.
loop.output: Short invitation or flyer copy with fixed event facts preserved.
loop.check: Compare dates, venue, prices and links with the brief; flag unsupported claims for editorial review.
loop.stop: One draft and one correction pass; missing facts or failed checks return to the assistant.
loop.why_not_simpler: Fresh audience-specific wording needs language generation; standard invitations use fixed templates without a model.

steps.what: Place the copy and assets into the required layouts.
Review the proof and approve its facts, wording and appearance.
Export approved versions and file the final production pack.

tasks.design: A configured event form in {WORKFLOW} supplies validated facts to reusable templates in {DOCS}. A bounded model loop drafts fresh wording only when needed; deterministic layout and export produce a proof and, after organiser approval, a versioned production pack.
tasks.previous_blocker: Event facts arrived piecemeal, wording varied, and each format required repeated manual layout and export.
tasks.enabler_now: Structured briefs and template rendering handle the repeatable work. Bounded drafting can produce wording variants cheaply, while AI-assisted coding reduces the cost of building the generator.
tasks.still_hard: Late changes, missing facts, unusual layouts, accessibility and print requirements still need care. A generated draft can contain unsupported wording.
tasks.human_edge: The organiser and assistant judge audience expectations, tone, visual clarity and whether the invitation makes a promise the event can meet.

ambition.what: An accessible event-material pack with coordinated invitation, flyer and plain-text versions.

tasks.altitude: The assistant handles fewer layout repetitions and can spend more time improving audience clarity and accessibility. Publication approval remains with the event organiser.

reach.task: Manage event-material dependencies and approval deadlines.
reach.learn: Maintain a brief, version history, change log and release checklist.

evidence.claim: The UK Department for Business and Trade evaluation observed drafting time savings and hallucinations; it does not establish savings for event materials.
Structured facts, fixed templates and deterministic export can handle routine material production without a model.
The step shares, remaining effort and build ranges are estimates for a small template-based pilot.

assumptions: Most requests fit a small set of approved invitation and flyer layouts.
The production pack is prepared for the organiser; audience selection and sending invitations are outside this task.
Fixed event facts are inserted from validated fields rather than regenerated.
Any correction after approval invalidates that approval before the next production export.
Approved assets have suitable usage rights. GDPR applies to any named speakers or contacts in the brief.
EU AI Act literacy duties apply to relevant staff use; this drafting workflow does not allocate tasks or monitor employees.
National consultation rules are checked where applicable. The build excludes recording meetings and employee usage dashboards.
Build ranges cover a few formats; external access or consultation delays may extend elapsed time.
unknowns: Which material formats, languages and brand templates are required.
Who approves facts, wording and final appearance.
Which accessibility and print specifications must be met.
Whether approved assets and document export interfaces are available.
What personal data, retention periods and local consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: How reliably do the chosen layouts handle long titles, translated copy and accessible reading order?
Which draft checks catch unsupported promises and changed event facts before approval?
new_work: Review generated wording and confirm unresolved event facts.
Maintain templates, fonts, asset permissions and export specifications.
Inspect unusual layouts and accessibility failures.
Invalidate outdated approvals when event details change.

role.altitude: The week shifts toward practical coaching, physical office support and checking exceptions. Routine preparation and record transfer shrink; spending, technical access and publication authority remain with their existing approvers.
reach: Help a computer systems analyst turn recurring user difficulties into reproducible requirements.
Help an inventory clerk investigate shortages and set replenishment thresholds.
Help a project management specialist coordinate event-material changes and approvals.
skills_to_grow: Design structured briefs, request forms and reusable templates.
Check model drafts against approved sources.
Configure simple workflows and recognise failed integrations.
Coach occasional users with accessible practice exercises.
Understand stock thresholds, version control and approval dependencies.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a small office-support service combining occasional-user coaching, weekly supply replenishment reviews and accessible event-material packs, supported by reusable forms and templates.

job.title: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
